summary_en: This phase II study tests cabozantinib together with nivolumab and ipilimumab in rare genitourinary tumors that have spread from where they started. Cabozantinib is taken by mouth, and nivolumab and ipilimumab are given through an IV; cycles repeat every 21 days for cycles 1-4 and every 28 days after that, for up to 2 years if the disease does not progress and side effects are not unacceptable. The main outcome measure is not stated; this is a phase II study.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase II evalúa cabozantinib junto con nivolumab e ipilimumab en tumores genitourinarios raros que se han diseminado desde su sitio de origen. El cabozantinib se toma por vía oral, y el nivolumab y el ipilimumab se administran por vena (IV); los ciclos se repiten cada 21 días en los ciclos 1 a 4 y cada 28 días después, durante hasta 2 años si la enfermedad no progresa y los efectos secundarios no son inaceptables. La medida de resultado principal no se indica; se trata de un estudio de fase II.
who_for: Metastatic rare genitourinary cancer shown on imaging or bone scan, with at least one measurable site of disease.
Histology that matches one of the listed cohorts, such as bladder, penile, kidney, urethral or prostate small cell tumors.
Karnofsky performance status of 80% or higher.
Up to 2 prior systemic anti-cancer treatments, or no prior treatment.
not_for: Prior treatment with both a MET or VEGF inhibitor and a PD-1, PD-L1 or CTLA-4 therapy.
Prior PD-1, PD-L1 or CTLA-4 therapy, except in urothelial carcinoma cohorts.
Active or acute diverticulitis, intra-abdominal abscess or GI obstruction within 12 months.
